result.topic_en: Euler shows that for a prime divisor 10p+1 the fifth-power residues number 2p, and that each residue arises from five distinct fifth powers. He then tabulates the fifth-power residues and the classes of non-residues for the primes 11 and 31.
result.transcription:
60 L. EULERI OPERA POSTHUMA. Arithmetica.
$c^2+cd+d^2+bc+bd+b^2+ac+ad+ab+a^2$,
$c^2+ce+e^2+bc+be+b^2+ac+ae+ab+a^2$,
harumque denuo differentia, quae per $d-e$ divisa est,
$e+d+c+b+a$.
477. Hinc apparet quinos numeros $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$, $e$, quorum potestates quintae, per numerum primum $10p+1$ divisae, paria relinquunt residua, ita esse comparatos, ut eorum summa
$a+b+c+d+e$
etiam per eundem sit divisibilis. Cum autem singuli minores sint quam $10p+1$, eorum summa est vel $10p+1$, vel $2(10p+1)$, vel $3(10p+1)$, vel $4(10p+1)$.
478. Cum numeros negativos etiam ut residua spectare liceat, haec summa $a+b+c+d+e$ ut nihilo aequalis considerari potest, unde datis quatuor $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$, quintus sponte datur, scilicet $e=-a-b-c-d$, qui cum sit unicus, patet plures quam quinque non dari.
479. En ergo novam demonstrationem, quod numerus residuorum diversorum pro quocunque divisore primo $2q+1$ sit vel $=2q$, vel $=\frac{2q}{5}$, et quod prius quidem semper eveniat, si $q$ non sit multiplum quinarii, posterius semper, si fuerit $q=5p$. Priori casu omnes numeri divisore minores sunt residua, posteriori tantum quinta eorum pars.
480. Posito igitur divisore primo $10p+1$, multitudo residuorum diversorum est $=2p$, inter quae cujusvis residui negativum quoque occurrit, ex quo eorum multitudo est par. Tum vero idem residuum quinque potestatibus diversis, quarum radices sint divisore minores, convenit, quas notasse juvabit.
481. Tales divisores cum sint 11, 31, 41, 61, 71, 101, etc. consideremus primo divisorem $10p+1=11$, quo fit $p=1$:
Residua | ex potestatibus | Classes non-residuorum I. II. III. IV.
1 | $1^5$, $3^5$, $4^5$, $5^5$, $9^5$ | 2 4 8 5
10 | $2^5$, $6^5$, $7^5$, $8^5$, $10^5$ | 9 7 3 6.
482. Sit divisor $10p+1=31$ et $p=3$, habebimus
Residua | ex potestatibus | Classes non-residuorum I. II. III. IV.
1 | $1^5$, $2^5$, $4^5$, $8^5$, $16^5$ | 2 4 8 16

26 | $3^5$, $6^5$, $12^5$, $17^5$, $24^5$ | 21 11 22 13
6 | $11^5$, $13^5$, $21^5$, $22^5$, $26^5$ | 12 24 17 3
25 | $5^5$, $9^5$, $10^5$, $18^5$, $20^5$ | 19 7 14 28
30 | $15^5$, $23^5$, $27^5$, $29^5$, $30^5$ | 29 27 23 15

methods.what: The sum of five numbers whose fifth powers leave equal residues modulo a prime 10p+1 is divisible by that prime
methods.quote:
quinos numeros $a$, $b$, $c$, $d$, $e$, quorum potestates quintae, per numerum primum $10p+1$ divisae, paria relinquunt residua, ita esse comparatos, ut eorum summa
$a+b+c+d+e$
etiam per eundem sit divisibilis

methods.what: Quotient of the difference of two symmetric polynomial expressions by d-e gives the sum a+b+c+d+e
methods.quote:
harumque denuo differentia, quae per $d-e$ divisa est,
$e+d+c+b+a$

methods.what: At most five fifth-power roots per residue: the fifth root is determined by the other four
methods.quote: $e=-a-b-c-d$, qui cum sit unicus, patet plures quam quinque non dari

methods.what: Number of distinct fifth-power residues mod a prime 2q+1 is 2q if 5 does not divide q, and 2q/5 if q=5p
methods.quote: numerus residuorum diversorum pro quocunque divisore primo $2q+1$ sit vel $=2q$, vel $=\frac{2q}{5}$, et quod prius quidem semper eveniat, si $q$ non sit multiplum quinarii, posterius semper, si fuerit $q=5p$

methods.what: For a prime 10p+1 there are 2p fifth-power residues, closed under negation, each the residue of five distinct fifth powers
methods.quote: multitudo residuorum diversorum est $=2p$, inter quae cujusvis residui negativum quoque occurrit

items.quote: Cum autem singuli minores sint quam $10p+1$, eorum summa est vel $10p+1$, vel $2(10p+1)$, vel $3(10p+1)$, vel $4(10p+1)$.
items.english: But since each is less than 10p+1, their sum is either 10p+1, or 2(10p+1), or 3(10p+1), or 4(10p+1).

items.quote: inter quae cujusvis residui negativum quoque occurrit, ex quo eorum multitudo est par
items.english: among which the negative of any residue also occurs, whence their number is even.

items.quote: Tum vero idem residuum quinque potestatibus diversis, quarum radices sint divisore minores, convenit, quas notasse juvabit.
items.english: Then the same residue belongs to five different powers whose roots are less than the divisor, and it will be useful to note these.
